newsitem.title: UK: C&W shares jump on Veba divorce terms.
newsitem.headline: C&W shares jump on Veba divorce terms.

text.p: Shares in Cable and Wireless Plc jumped at the start of trade on Friday after the terms of its widely-expected divorce from a partnership with German utility Veba AG were announced.
The shares opened 7-1/2p firmer at 483p at 0830 GMT.
C&W said it would sell its 45 percent stake in Vebacom, its joint venture with Veba, for 2.21 billion marks, and buy out Veba's half of Cable and Wireless Europe SA for 90 million.
It said the deal would be enhance earnings in the financial year to end-March 1998 and would create an exceptional pre-tax profit of around 60 million stg in the current financial year.
Vebacom will hold on to its 10.4 percent stake in C&W and hold discussions with C&W before selling any part of the stake.

"It's good news for the market in the sense that Veba will hold on to their 10.4 percent stake for the time being at least and inform C&W before disposing of it," Nikko Europe analyst Dennis Exton said. "That's reassuring -- there won't be 10.4 percent of 2.2 billion shares hitting the market unannounced."
He said the price C&W received for its Vebacom stake was "fairly good".
"It's a fair get-out price. From C&W's point of view they couldn't have hoped for more," Exton said.
Steve Scruton, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, said he was positive about the deal and remained a buyer of the stock.
"The concern was how much money they were going to end up investing in Vebacom and was it going to be a bottomless pit," Scruton said.

"They're walking away from their share of the losses and on broad brush figures, they could be 120 million stg or so better off next year, maybe more," he said. "So you could be talking about an increase of 10 percent in next year's pre-tax profits."
He was also positive on the price C&W got for its Vebacom stake: "They got above assets, which is good."

C&W said it was leaving the German alliance to concentrate on the development of C&W Communications, a cable firm formed through the merger of its Mercury unit with Nynex Corp's Nynex Cablecomms and Videotron Holdings Plc.
But analysts continued to speculate that C&W would enter a global telecoms alliance, with the Global One partnership of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint Corp of the U.S.
"I think it might happen in two stages," said Exton at Nikko Europe.
"You'll see first the pledging of C&W Europe and then the pledging of key business areas like the UK and Asia into something major like Global One," he said.
Scruton said he was bullish about C&W chief executive Richard Brown's strategy.
"I think what Brown is doing is very good -- he's focusing on the areas of the world he understands," Scruton said.
He said a deal with another telecoms player was likely, but the identity of the partner remained in question.
"Given that Brown comes from a very strong North American telecoms background he may have ambitions there," Scruton said.
"He could be doing things with Sprint, he could be talking to one of the Bells. And Nynex has been mentioned too as a possible partner."
-- Andrew Marshall, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
